Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at LoftPay is excited about the latency profile we saw. We're at the stage where procurement and engineering want a short pilot to validate cost savings for two specific flows: (1) user-facing chat (avg prompt+response ~ 1.2k tokens, high p95 latency sensitivity) and (2) nightly batch embedding for fraud models (large bulk jobs).

Two asks from our side to move forward quickly:
- Can you recommend a quantization + runtime config for a 13B-class model that balances p95 latency (~<250ms) and token unit cost? We're currently evaluating int8 vs 4-bit variants and would like your operational recommendation (KV cache, batching settings, expected tokens/sec).
- Would Redwood consider a small, time-boxed pilot credit package with a discounted trial (we're thinking 75k inference tokens + 300k embedding units) while we run integration tests? Procurement wants draft terms to start internal approvals.

I've attached a short evaluation profile (loftpay_eval_profile.csv) with our expected QPS/seq-length distribution. Happy to hop on a call if you prefer.

Hi Elena — thanks for the profile and for outlining the two flows. Quick answers up front, then a proposed pilot package.

Technical recommendation (13B-class workloads):
- Quantization: q4f (4-bit, per-channel floating-point aware calibration) for best latency/cost tradeoff on our runtime. It keeps latency close to int8 for generative loops while saving 25–40% on token compute compared to full precision.
- KV caching: enable prefix KV cache for chat sessions (TTL ~ 30m) — you'll get large savings on repeated context.
- Batching: start with continuous-batching enabled, target batch_max = 12–16 for real-time endpoints to keep p95 ~200–250ms at your expected QPS. For large nightly embedding jobs, use batch_max = 64+ and parallel workers.
- Expected economics: with q4f + prefix caching we estimate pilot effective tokens/unit cost ~0.0009 USD/token for generation (varies by sequence length) — embedding unit economics separate (we'll break that out in the pricing table).

Pilot proposal (time-boxed):
- Duration: 3 weeks (integration + smoke + ops run).
- Credits: Redwood trial credits covering 75k inference tokens + 300k embedding units (as requested) plus 3 days of engineering support/enablement.
- Deliverables: pilot scope doc, cost/runbook, and a short evaluation call at EOW 3.

I've attached a short pilot scope draft (pilot_scope.pdf) and our suggested pricing table (pricing_table_v2.xlsx). If this looks good I can loop in Aditya on commercials and get a DocuSign MOU prepared.

Best,
Sofia
